Ok, now on to the question. It seems my computer isn't as fast as it used to be. Now, I see three possible reasons: 1. Malware 2. Time to reinstall Windows, and 3. Need to clean out dust. I don't think it's reason 1 because I take a few steps to prevent it (Ad Block, Malwarebytes, Windows Defender, etc.) But I think it's either reason 2 or 3. I haven't done either of these since I recieved my computer (1 year ago.)
Is it time to clean the dust out of my computer?
Well cleaning out the dust definitely couldn't hurt. And if it's still slow after that, then reinstall.

Dust can block the fine CPU cooling channels and thus heating up your processor. Use a flashlight to see if any dust is collected inside the cooling fins. The processor will slow down because of that to prevent overheating. You should definitely open the computer and check for dust.

I opened mine up a few weeks ago and cleaned everything inside. I have no issues with overheating now and everything seems to be running faster. Whether this is your issue or not, it is probably a good idea to clean out all of the dust before something breaks.

Check the speed with a CPU monitor rather than relying on visible indicators such as program performance. I recommend using Microsoft's SysInternals utilities package. There are many utils that will help you localize the issue.

I've been using them for years and found them indispensable.

Disclaimer: I hate microsoft.

Identifying and removing malware is its own art form, but not necessarily the problem. Before reinstalling Windows, there is a lot of cleanup you can do. First go through your Programs and Features and just uninstall crap that you don't want or use, and then disable superfluous startup programs (I'm looking at you, adobe and apple); this is done either in msconfig or the task manager depending on your Windows version. Run the Windows cleanup tool, and CCleaner (both for temp files and registry cleaning) then defrag your drive. Don't defrag SSDs, though, as it just reduces the life of the drive and provides zero performance improvement.

Good luck!

If you think it's dust, what you are really saying is you think your computer is overheating and dynamically slowing its system clock in order to compensate, which I sincerely doubt. What PCs will do, however, is sense the temp and increase fan speed to compensate, or simply shut down/lock up. Cleaning out the dust won't hurt, but I doubt it will help the problem you describe. I would reinstall windows.

As a side note, there are free software out there to report back fan speed and temp sensor readings. Speedfan is one that comes to mind.

“Really?” he asked. “Because from where I’m standing it looks pretty simple.” He reached over and touched the bra strap that was hanging out of my top, and I realized that both cups were showing where they’d been pushed up over my chest.
“Shit,” I said. “Look, it’s not like that... “
“Like what?”
“I mean, I’m not some kind of… you know, street girl. I was just at a friend’s apartment, and things got… weird.”
Chris frowned. “Do I need to have someone come round and talk to your ‘friend’? Maybe someone with a badge and a gun?”
“No!” I held up my hands. “It’s okay. I’ll work it out. I just have to find…” I coughed, and suddenly I was crying again. “God dammit…”
Chris stepped in again, wrapping his arms around me. “Hey, hey, I’m sorry,” he said softly. “I didn’t mean to make it worse. Come on, let’s get you out of the rain and you can dry off, then I’ll take you home.”

Everyday, sometimes more than once a day (and usually on my drive home from work when I'm looking forward to something to eat that evening) I ask myself this question....'What have I eaten today?' I can usually calculate to within a tolerance of 50 or so calories everything I have eaten and I mean EVERYTHING...not a 'salad' where the dressing did not count because it was only on the side, not those few sneaky biscuits that don't count because no-one saw, not a chocolate bar that didn't count because I was standing up when I ate it, not the 'healthy' vegetables brushed with butter that didn't count, not a piece of birthday cake I only ate because it would have been rude to refuse.....EVERYTHING. I know that I maintain weight on around 1800 calories per day so if I've had close to that I cut down what I have that evening, or the next day to compensate - I do not delude myself that I've stuck to a certain number of calories when clearly I have not. Obviously, I love the cake and biscuits as much as anyone else but they all come with consequences which I am happy to recognise before they begin to make an obvious difference.
